description: We are students from Egypt joining NASA Space Apps 2026! We're building Challenge 5 - AstroHealth, a dashboard to monitor astronaut vitals (heart rate, oxygen, sleep) with alerts. We have web dev & UI/UX skills and a simple MVP plan. Looking for Frontend dev, designer, or any space enthusiast. Beginners welcome!
summary:
Our project, "Astronaut Health Monitoring System" is a software tool made to keep track of astronauts’ health while they're on space missions. Space is an environment. It has microgravity, levels of radiation, and conditions that can change the body. It also brings isolation, which can affect how astronauts feel and function.

We built a platform that collects key health data. It watches heart rate, blood oxygen levels (SpO₂), body temperature, blood pressure, and breathing rate. The system checks this data for changes. When it sees something, it sends out an alert. This helps catch health problems. It also shows health trends in a dashboard. This way astronauts and doctors on Earth can stay informed. Respond quickly.

This project matters a lot. Detecting health issues early lets medical teams make decisions. It makes astronauts safer. It helps make long space missions more successful.
details:
Our project is an "Astronaut Health Monitoring System" designed to address the health challenges astronauts face during space missions, especially long-duration missions. It provides a digital platform that organizes and analyzes health-related data to help identify unusual changes and support early intervention.

The system presents important health indicators through a user-friendly dashboard, helping users understand health trends, recognize potential abnormalities, and monitor astronauts' conditions. By making health information easier to interpret, the project aims to support better medical decision-making, improve astronaut safety, and contribute to the success of future space missions.

Our team used NASA data as a scientific reference for the project and Replit as our development environment. We also used Claude and ChatGPT as AI-assisted tools to support research, problem-solving, and development.

The creative aspect of our project is its application of digital health monitoring to the unique challenges of space exploration. We considered the effects of the space environment, data reliability, accessibility, user experience, and the importance of early detection. Our goal is to create a practical and expandable solution that can support safer human exploration beyond Earth.
